title: Gateway cleanup scheduled task flashes a console window every minute and steals keyboard focus
subtitle: openclaw/openclaw-windows-node #1887
author: jpink
body:
﻿## Summary

The Windows Hub registers a per-user scheduled task that runs `cleanup.ps1` **every minute**. Although the action passes `-WindowStyle Hidden`, a console window visibly flashes on each run and **steals keyboard focus** from the foreground application. Because the Hub re-registers the task on every start, users cannot persistently disable or fix it.

## Environment

- Windows 11 Business, build 26300
- OpenClaw (Microsoft Store) `2026.10.502.0`
- OpenClawGateway package `2026.10.600.0`
- Windows Terminal set as the default terminal application

## Details

Task name: `OpenClaw Gateway cleanup - <SID> - OpenClawFoundation.OpenClaw_rfcbke2p71se2`

- Triggers: time trigger repeating every `PT1M`, plus logon trigger
- Principal: current user, `LogonType Interactive`
- Action:
  ```
  powershell.exe -NoProfile -NonInteractive -WindowStyle Hidden -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File "%USERPROFILE%\.openclaw-companion\cleanup\OpenClawFoundation.OpenClaw_rfcbke2p71se2\cleanup.ps1" -Family OpenClawFoundation.OpenClaw_rfcbke2p71se2
  ```

`powershell.exe` is a console subsystem executable, so Windows creates a console (here hosted by Windows Terminal) before PowerShell can apply `-WindowStyle Hidden`. The result is a brief visible window every minute that takes focus — typing into another app is interrupted.

While the Companion package is installed, the script exits immediately with result `0`, so in normal operation each run only spawns PowerShell to query AppX packages and exit.

After a reboot, the Hub re-registers the task in its original form (`Register-CleanupTask` uses `-Force`), so disabling the task or editing its action does not persist.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Install the Store build of Windows Hub and complete local Gateway setup.
2. Ensure Windows Terminal is the default terminal (Windows 11 default).
3. Work in any other application — a window flashes about once per minute and focus is lost.

## Expected

Background maintenance runs without any visible window and never steals focus.

## Workaround

Wrapping the action with a headless console host removes the window entirely while the task still completes with result `0`:

```
conhost.exe --headless "C:\Windows\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe" -NoProfile -NonInteractive -WindowStyle Hidden -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File "...\cleanup.ps1" -Family OpenClawFoundation.OpenClaw_rfcbke2p71se2
```

Since the Hub re-registers the task on start, keeping this applied currently requires a separate user task that rewrites the action periodically.

## Suggestions

1. Launch the cleanup headlessly (`conhost.exe --headless`, a windowless host, or a GUI-subsystem launcher) instead of relying on `-WindowStyle Hidden`.
2. Reconsider the 1-minute polling interval — detecting package removal could run at logon only, at a much longer interval, or react to AppX deployment events.
3. Avoid overwriting an existing task's action/settings on every Hub start, so administrator/user adjustments survive.

comments.body:
Closing the installed cleanup-task flash bug as fixed by #1782 (fix(setup): stop console flashes when Gateway cleanup runs), merged as ef1df54dfe95a8b0a2ae8033425561136d8a70ef and included in v2026.11.1. The task now uses a durable GUI helper with creation-time CreateNoWindow; the PR records positive-control and before/after Scheduler observations, including x64 and ARM64 cleanup behavior. The correction is in Companion, not a Gateway-only update, and normal Companion startup refreshes its registered task. #2056 (fix(setup): clean uninstall leaves a Gateway cleanup task running) separately tracks orphaned tasks after clean-uninstall and is not being closed here. Store rollout/version acceptance and broader SAC policy proof remain distinct release checks.

Release: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/releases/tag/v2026.11.1
